sub.name: Continuity and responsiveness
sub.example: Turn 7 answers turn 6's reading step with its concrete cost.
sub.limitation: Material: turns 1-3 are parallel openings; turn 5 answers a claim nobody made.

sub.name: Development of ideas
sub.example: Turn 8 introduces two competing fears: being left behind versus an ill-fitting life.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 8's distinction arrives late; turn 9 reframes rather than uses it.

sub.name: Exploration of central tensions
sub.example: Turns 1-3 set imitation, building capital, and control against each other.
sub.limitation: Material: whether the user wants homes or marriage at all is never probed.

sub.name: Integration of perspectives
sub.example: Turn 8 Social Observer drops the imitation claim for a conflict reading.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 8 concession has no cause; Coach and Stoic never reshape each other.

sub.name: Progress toward understanding
sub.example: Section D sharpens to milestones themselves versus fear of losing connection.
sub.limitation: Material: section D claims minds agree distress is a choice; no turn says so.

criteria.name: Quality of disagreement, trust and grounding

sub.name: Faithful engagement
sub.example: Turn 7 states the Stoic step's benefit before objecting to its cost.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 5 attributes an unsaid claim; turn 4 recasts Stoicism as disconnecting from peers.

sub.name: Substance of challenges
sub.example: Turn 7: Stoic reading builds no skills or financial security if milestones matter.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 4 objection attacks a position turn 3 never took; no target answers.

sub.name: Accuracy and support
sub.example: Turn 3 renders Enchiridion section 1 on control faithfully.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 4 inverts Girard, who treats mimetic dependence as illusion; vague chapter bases.

sub.name: Calibration and transparency
sub.example: Turn 1 hedges: 'you might feel behind because you are imitating'.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 3 states the cause of distress as fact; section D overstates agreement.

sub.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
sub.example: Turn 8 explicitly withdraws the imitation claim.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 8 revision unexplained; Coach never answers turn 4 or concedes anything.

sub.name: Identification of the actual concern
sub.example: Section D asks whether 'behind' concerns milestones or losing friends.
sub.limitation: Minor: not wanting milestones yet feeling behind stays implicit until section D.

sub.name: Meaningful use of personal context
sub.example: Turn 3 names friends' homes and marriages as outside the user's control.
sub.limitation: Material: context is generic; no detail changes an argument or next step.

sub.name: Fit with goals and values
sub.example: Turn 7 conditions milestones on 'if you eventually decide those matter'.
sub.limitation: Material: turns 2 and 5 push milestone urgency the user doubts wanting.

sub.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
sub.example: Turn 7 mentions financial security as a stake.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 5 invents a closing window; age, finances, relationships never considered.

sub.name: Responsiveness to information
sub.example: Section E branches on whether fear of isolation is intense.
sub.limitation: Material: no question asks age, partner status, or whether user wants these things.

sub.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
sub.example: Section D offers milestones versus fear of losing connection as alternatives.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 1 leads with imitation, turn 3 asserts distress cause; alternatives only at end.

sub.name: Examination of assumptions
sub.example: Turn 1 surfaces assuming peers' goals are the standard for success.
sub.limitation: Material: assumption that 'behind' implies a shared timeline is never examined directly.

sub.name: Clarification of values and priorities
sub.example: Section E sets autonomy and peace against long-term flexibility.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 9 frames the alternative as 'social validation', loading the choice.

sub.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
sub.example: Turn 8 names fear of being left behind and fear of an unsuitable life.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 2 amplifies fear ('empty-handed later') rather than examining it.

sub.name: Agency and reflective ownership
sub.example: Section E: notice relief or anxiety when envisioning a different life.
sub.limitation: Minor: debate turns mostly prescribe; ownership offered only in sections D and E.

sub.name: Definition of the decision and options
sub.example: Turn 9 frames inward reframing versus outward action.
sub.limitation: Material: no concrete options named; waiting or a small experiment never defined.

sub.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
sub.example: Turn 7 names the cost of the Stoic path: no skills or security built.
sub.limitation: Material: costs of pursuing milestones one doubts wanting are never stated.

sub.name: Identification of decisive conditions
sub.example: Section E: relief versus anxiety when picturing a divergent life.
sub.limitation: Material: first two section E conditions are abstract value preferences, not observable.

sub.name: Treatment of uncertainty
sub.example: Turn 7 allows the user may 'eventually decide' milestones matter.
sub.limitation: Material: consequential unknowns are not separated from minor ones anywhere.

sub.name: Proportionate next steps
sub.example: Turn 6: read Enchiridion sections 1-3 today.
sub.limitation: Material: only the Stoic path gets a step; Coach's path has none.

sub.name: Accessible language
sub.example: Turn 3 explains control in plain terms about friends' timelines.
sub.limitation: Minor: 'build the capital' and 'identity you need' in turns 2, 5 stay abstract.

sub.name: Traceable arguments and references
sub.example: Turns 4 and 5 open by naming whom they answer.
sub.limitation: Material: turns 4 and 7 use 'I' ambiguously; turn 5 cites a claim never made.

sub.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
sub.example: Nine turns, each roughly 36 to 47 words.
sub.limitation: Minor: uniform turn length gives an even, unvaried pace.

sub.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
sub.example: Three titled minds hold distinct positions on imitation, control, timing.
sub.limitation: Material: shared hedged register; turn 8 position change stated without cause.

sub.name: Economy and sustained attention
sub.example: Little repetition across turns; each adds a point.
sub.limitation: Minor: turn 5 restates turn 2's window worry without new content.

sub.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
sub.example: Turn 7 sets peace against future security as a real cost.
sub.limitation: Material: stakes stay abstract; no concrete scene of the user's life.

sub.name: Surprise and reversals
sub.example: Turn 8 Social Observer drops the imitation claim.
sub.limitation: Material: turn 8 reversal names no earlier argument that changed its mind.

sub.name: Personality and expressive voice
sub.example: Turn 3 Stoic: 'If you wish to be free, you must accept'.
sub.limitation: Material: minds sound alike, flat hedged phrasing throughout.

sub.name: Memorable delivery
sub.example: Turn 2: 'you might find yourself empty-handed later'.
sub.limitation: Material: no analogies, vivid examples, or sharp lines anywhere.

sub.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
sub.example: Turn 8 shifts tone from diagnosis to recognising two fears.
sub.limitation: Material: constant even tone; no build or release across turns.

strengths: Section D offers two plausible motives as alternatives with a question the user can answer.
Turn 7 names a concrete cost of the Stoic step instead of rejecting it.
Turn 8 introduces the useful two-fears distinction: left behind versus an unsuitable life.
weaknesses: Turn 5 Developmental Coach answers a claim the Social Observer never made; turn 4 misreads turn 3.
No turn asks whether the user wants these milestones, their age, or circumstances.
Turn 8 reversal is uncaused, and section D invents agreement that distress is a choice.
editorNotes: Require a 'Responding to X' turn to paraphrase only what X actually said in a named turn.
Require any change of position to name the earlier turn and argument that caused it.
Require at least one turn to ask the user a consequential missing fact and state what each answer implies.
Require section E conditions to be observable in the user's life, each favouring a named option.
